=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- README.md:"Roll back @stable" section, the paragraph added by the last run: "The rollback only cancels promote runs that are queued or running when it starts." | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: This sentence does not match `scripts/rollback_stable.sh`. `cancel_new_release_runs` runs once in the first pass and again on every drain poll, so promote, release and auto-release runs that become active before the drain finishes are cancelled too. Only runs the poller dispatches after the rollback has exited are not cancelled.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime. The operator runbook gets the covered window wrong. Suggested wording: "The rollback cancels promote runs that are queued or running until it finishes draining; a promote run the poller dispatches after that is not cancelled."
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "After a rollback, neither `auto-release-stable.yml` nor the `promote-main-to-stable.yml` cycle releases until a release is cut deliberately."
  Expected change site: The `promote` job of `.github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml` (the job at line 155: it checks `target_sha`, fast-forwards `stable`, then runs "Dispatch test-and-mark-stable on stable" at line 403), or the poller step in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` that dispatches it with `target_sha`.
  Evidence of absence: The hold is checked only in the scheduled `cycle` path (`scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh`, step "0. Stable rollback hold"). No hunk touches the `promote` job or the poller dispatch. The README paragraph confirms the gap: a poller-dispatched `promote` can fast-forward `stable`, and the release's "Clear stable rollback hold" step then clears the hold. The only safeguard is the operator manually removing `ai:comprehensive-test-pending`, which runs against §20. The issue does not defer this case. The editor deferred it because of the `files_touched` grant. This needs a follow-up issue or an explicit operator decision.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- HARDENING: scripts/rollback_stable.sh `cancel_new_release_runs`, the else branch that prints "Could not cancel ... retrying on the next poll." When the cancel fails because the run finished (409), the warning wrongly says the cancel will be retried. Fix: reword it to "Could not cancel $1 run ${active_id}; it is retried on the next poll if still active." (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

  WHY: scripts/rollback_stable.sh (lines 399-418) runs a drain loop that polls and cancels newly active release and promote runs for up to STABLE_ROLLBACK_CANCEL_WAIT_SECS. The documentation leaves that continued coverage out.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- README.md:line 4778, the sentence "The rollback only cancels promote runs that are queued or running when it starts." | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sentence does not match scripts/rollback_stable.sh. The drain loop calls cancel_new_release_runs on every poll until STABLE_ROLLBACK_CANCEL_WAIT_SECS, so promote, release and auto-release runs that become active during the drain are cancelled too. "when it starts" is inaccurate.
  WHY: An operator may believe a run that became active during the rollback is safe when it was in fact cancelled. The wording should describe the drain-window coverage and explicitly carve out runs dispatched after the drain ends.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "After a rollback, neither `auto-release-stable.yml` nor the `promote-main-to-stable.yml` cycle releases until a release is cut deliberately."
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml`'s `promote` job, or the poller dispatch path in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (or `scripts/comprehensive_promotion_gate_before_final_merge`).
  Evidence of absence: Only the scheduled cycle in `scripts/promote_main_cycle.sh` is gated, plus cancellation of promote runs active at rollback start. The poller-dispatched `promote` job is not gated. With `ai:comprehensive-test-pending` set at rollback time, the poller can dispatch `promote` with `target_sha` and fast-forward `stable`, and the release clears the hold via the "Clear stable rollback hold" step in `test-and-mark-stable.yml` / `mark-stable.yml`. README lines 4774-4781 document the gap and the manual label removal.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- README.md:line 4778 ("The rollback only cancels promote runs that are queued or running when it starts.") | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The sentence does not match the script. `cancel_new_release_runs` is called in the first pass (scripts/rollback_stable.sh:397) and on every drain poll (scripts/rollback_stable.sh:408, inside the drain loop at lines 400-418). Runs that become active during the drain window (`STABLE_ROLLBACK_CANCEL_WAIT_SECS`, default 300s) are cancelled too. `tests/test_rollback_stable.py::test_release_run_started_during_drain_is_cancelled` proves it.
  WHY: No runtime failure. The runbook mixes up the poller-dispatch-after-rollback case with runs cancelled during the drain. Suggested wording: "The rollback cancels only the promote runs that are queued or running before it finishes draining; a promote run the poller dispatches after that is not cancelled."
- TASK COMPLETENESS / INTENT GAPS: NONE. The reviewer considers the earlier poller-dispatched `promote` hold gap addressed by the documented mitigation in README.md:4774-4781, by the issue's §18.E scope (hold check only in `promote_main_cycle.sh`), and by the `files_touched` grant that excludes `promote-main-to-stable.yml` / `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`.
- Other categories: NONE. The reviewer verified these against the code: hold routing at scripts/rollback_stable.sh:299-304 / :303, the cancel-retry change at scripts/rollback_stable.sh:383-387, and the `target_input` regex validation.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
